D015-D007_h001.question:
It started a little over a year ago. I’ve been pretty much constantly low since then—like this heavy, gray feeling that doesn’t really lift. I used to be on top of my graduate work, but now even opening my laptop feels impossible. I miss deadlines, and I just stare at articles without taking anything in. My head feels foggy, like I’m thinking through cotton; I lose my train of thought mid-sentence in seminars.

I’ve thought a lot about ending things. Not just vague thoughts—I’ve pictured exactly how and where I’d do it, and I’ve gone over the details in my head more times than I want to admit.

On top of that, there are these…other things. For most of this year, while I’ve been depressed, I’ve also heard a man’s voice commenting on what I do, especially when I’m studying or trying to sleep. And I’ve had these strong convictions that I’m meant to be some kind of groundbreaking scientist, that I have a special role in changing the field, even though objectively my life is kind of falling apart.

What really scares me is that a couple of months ago, for about two or three weeks, my mood actually felt almost normal—I wasn’t particularly sad—but the voice and those “I’m destined for greatness” beliefs kept going just the same.
D015-D007_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h002.question:

My mind feels foggy most of the time. Simple things like reviewing spreadsheets or making decisions take way more effort, and I lose my train of thought in meetings. It’s affecting my work and my marriage — my wife says I seem distant and “blank.”

Some days, especially commuting, I get these sudden urges to just step in front of a train or off a platform. I don’t plan it out, but the impulse can be really strong and scary.

On top of that, I’ve become convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body — like my organs are rotting — even though doctors say all my tests are fine. I sometimes feel things crawling or moving under my skin when nothing’s there. Those sensations and beliefs have come and gone, and there was a stretch a couple of weeks where that stuff was happening even when my mood wasn’t particularly low, just kind of neutral. But for most of this year, the numb, depressed state has been the main backdrop to everything.
D015-D007_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

On top of that, I’m convinced something catastrophic is coming, like the world is about to collapse or already has and everyone’s pretending. I’ll feel things crawling on my skin, like bugs or fingers tapping me, when there’s nothing there.
